newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate edges down at close on liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate edges down at close on liquidity.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed down five basis points at 21.20 percent on Monday as ample liquidity eased upside pressure caused by a weaker peso, traders said.
"It was a dull session, under some pressure from a soft peso and zigzagging U.S. long bond yields," a trader said.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed 2.25 centavos weaker at 7.8370/7.8400 per dollar.
Yields on U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds increased to 6.94 percent in late trade, compared to 6.89 percent on Friday.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed up 10 basis points at 23.35 percent.
Despite upside pressures on secondary rates, dealers said the market had sufficient liquidity for overnight rates to close down.
Banco de Mexico drained liquidity from the market by auctioning three credits totaling 2.614 billion pesos, which it assigned at between 23.20 and 24.75 percent.
Dealers said turnover was low for the session, a sign of market caution ahead of the primary auction on Tuesday.
"Some of us expect an uptick in rates this week. Nonetheless, it remains to be seen what happens in the foreign exchange and money markets tomorrow,' a dealer said.
Bellwether 28-day Cetes (Treasury Certificates) rates were assigned at 22.93 percent at last week's auction.
Liquidity of 1.419 billion pesos was expected to return to the market on Tuesday.
